My dear [Miss Sewell](/person/1305)[^2]

I have been from home or I would have answered sooner. I send you a pound for the poor woman—which I hope may help her on a little while.

Pray thank [the Warden](/person/1304) greatly for his very kind messages through [Mr Wither](/person/1544). If my friend [Miss Peard](/person/1160)[^3] can come, I am sure you will like her. She is an excellent singer among other perfections, and full of life and brightness. I think you will like her book One Year. Her home is Torquay, I believe the family is Cornish and the [Garibaldi man](/person/1159) is her uncle. [^4] Did you ever try how many words can be made out of the letters of Triangle? and do you know the

[part of letter missing]

I am hoping soon to see [your sister](/person/1301)
Yours very sincerely

C M Yonge


[^2]: Name partly erased.
[^3]: Name partly erased.
[^4]: John Whitehead Peard (1811-1880), known as \'Garibaldi\'s Englishman\', who had fought with Garibaldi in Italy, was Peard’s uncle and lived in Cornwall.
